text: [mysterious] This is Max. You can't see him. Nobody can. [excited] For the next twenty-four hours, Max is invisible. Free movies. Free food. Zero consequences. [deadpan] Dave has been screaming for six minutes. [pause] There's just one problem. Max can't see either. [tense] And by hour nine... it nearly kills him.

[excited] Hour one. Max does what everyone says they'd do. He watches three films. Back to back. Front row. For free. [sarcastic] Max, I know you're in here. I can hear you chewing. Hour two. Revenge. He taps Dave on the shoulder. Then the other shoulder. Then both. Dave has now moved house. Hour three. The ultimate test. Mum. [deadpan] Mum does not scream. Mum just says, "Put it back, Max." [warm] Some powers are no match for mums. Hour three and a half. Max photobombs fifty selfies. [deadpan] Every single photo shows a pair of sunglasses doing peace signs.

[curious] But here's the part every superhero movie gets wrong. To be invisible, light has to go straight through you. In one side... out the other. But your eyes only work by catching light. The back of your eye has to absorb it to see anything. Invisible eyes can't catch anything. The light just... keeps going. And being see-through isn't enough anyway. A glass of water is see-through. You can still see it. That's because glass and water bend light. To be truly invisible, every part of you has to bend light exactly like air does. Not a tiny bit more. [pause] So the second Max turned invisible... He went completely blind. [sarcastic] Which explains why he walked into that cinema wall. Twice. And it's true in nature too. Every see-through animal on Earth, glass frogs, glass squid, baby eels, still has visible eyes. Because eyes that light passes through... don't work. [playful] If you'd still pick invisibility after hearing that, smash like. If not... we're judging you.

Hour four. Max tries to get home. He uses a stick. Then he realises nobody can see the stick's owner, so the stick looks haunted. So he tries something smarter. Clicking. Like a bat. This is real. Some blind people navigate by clicking their tongue and listening to the echoes. They can ride bikes doing it. [deadpan] Max is not one of those people yet. Max clicks straight into a lamppost. Hour five. Lunch. [disgusted] Here's something else they don't tell you. Food is only invisible once your body has digested it. So for two hours... Max is a floating, half-chewed sandwich. Hour six. He's freezing. Sunlight warms you because your skin soaks it up. Max's doesn't. The sunshine goes straight through him. [deadpan] It's thirty degrees. Max is wearing three coats. Hour seven. Only one living thing can find him. Sir Biscuit doesn't need to see Max. Sir Biscuit can smell Max. From two streets away. [warm] Good boy. [tense] Hour eight. Max is lost, blind, and he has no idea it's getting dark.

[tense] Hour nine. Max reaches a road. He can't see the traffic. And here's the real problem... The traffic can't see him either. [urgent] Max steps out. [shouting] Max! [pause] He's pulled back by the one friend who always knew where he was. [shaky] Every year, more than a million people die on the world's roads. Being seen is half of staying alive.

[sarcastic] Hour ten. Having nearly died, Max makes a sensible, grown-up decision. He's going to rob a bank. He follows a guard through three locked doors, holding onto the back of his belt. The vault door closes. Max is inside. Surrounded by millions. [pause] And he can't see a single note. [deadpan] Max has stolen a stapler. [tense] But it doesn't matter. Because the bank already knows he's there. Here's the thing. Max is invisible to the light our eyes see. But every warm body glows with heat. Infrared. Thermal cameras see that glow. Snakes like pit vipers can hunt in the dark with it. [deadpan] So on the bank's thermal camera, Max is the brightest thing in the building. [excited] Max runs. Blind. Through a bank. Holding a stapler. Hour twelve. Escaped. But then... it rains. Every raindrop that hits Max splashes off him. And suddenly there's a perfect water outline of a man standing in the street. [deadpan] Being invisible only works on dry days. Max is from Manchester. Hour fourteen. Back home, soaked, Max asks Dave how he looks. Dave says, quote, "Like a scarf that's having a really bad day." [quiet] And that's when it hits him. The worst part of being invisible isn't the danger.

[quiet] Hour seventeen. Max sits in the park. People walk past. Nobody looks. It turns out being invisible isn't a superpower. It's what lonely already feels like. He calls his friends. They hear his voice and see nobody. They think it's a prank and hang up. Hour twenty. Mum leaves a plate out. With a note. [warm] He eats every single one. You can see all of them. Hour twenty-three. Max counts down. Three. Two. One...

[excited] So scientists try to fix him. Keep the invisibility, bring back the eyes. Like a glass frog. Invisible skin. Invisible muscle. Working eyes. [pause] They forgot about the skeleton. [deadpan] Mum screamed this time. [laughing] Max is now the only person in town who can see perfectly... and still can't go outside.
What's the first thing you'd do if you were invisible? Wrong answers only. Comments are open. [sarcastic] And Max, put the popcorn down. I can hear you.
